name: Southeast Ridge

waypoints.name: Boston Basin Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive Cascade River Road about 21.7 miles from Marblemount to the unsigned Boston Basin pullout, at roughly 3,200-3,400 feet - getting this far depends on the road being open past a washout further up. Park at the small, unsigned roadside pullout; there's no trailhead sign. Camping in Boston Basin requires an NPS wilderness permit, since it's a quota area, arranged through Marblemount.

waypoints.name: Boston Basin
waypoints.directions: From the pullout, walk the old Diamond Mine roadbed for about three quarters of a mile, then turn sharp right onto the steep climbers' trail. It climbs through old growth across four stream crossings to treeline near 5,300 ft and the low camps, then continues up open heather and slabs to the higher camp on the meadow knoll.

waypoints.name: Base of southeast ridge
waypoints.directions: From camp, skirt the climber's-left side of the Quien Sabe Glacier and gain it high, then rope up and traverse east along the top of the glacier until you are directly beneath the tower. Climb the single gully that breaks the rock band there (snow early season, loose scree later) to a terrace at the tower's base, then a short second gully to the notch. If your gully does not lead onto a terrace directly under the fin, you are in the wrong one.

waypoints.name: Sharkfin Tower summit
waypoints.directions: From the notch, skirt the ridge on climber's right over large blocks and up a short dihedral to the crest, then follow the exposed crest and the upper blocks for about three pitches of low fifth class to the small summit.

approach: From the Boston Basin climbers' trailhead on Cascade River Road (~3,200–3,400 ft, ~21.7 mi from Marblemount when the road is open past the washout), pick up the unmaintained but well-worn Boston Basin climbers' path. It switchbacks steeply up through forest on old roadbed/boot path, crosses a couple of small streams (last reliable water before camp), and breaks out of the trees onto open meadow slabs. Expect roughly 3.2 mi and 2,500 ft of gain to the designated low camp (~5,300–5,700 ft), about 2.5–3 hours for a laden party; the high camp sits higher still on a meadow knoll around 6,300–6,400 ft and shaves real time off the summit day. From camp, contour/ascend slabs and easy snowfields on the left (climber's) side of the Quien Sabe Glacier toward Sharkfin Col, rope up for glacier travel, and traverse east along the top of the glacier for several hundred feet until you're directly beneath the tower's obvious approach gully. This gully runs 35° snow in early season and degrades to loose class 2–3 scree/rubble by late summer; crampons and an axe (or trekking poles once it's melted out) help. Follow it up to a notch/terrace at the base of the southeast ridge proper. Route-finding here is the crux of the approach and has real consequences: a fatal 2005 accident on this peak began when a party climbed a similar-looking but incorrect gully next to the standard line, so confirm you're in the correct gully (directly below the ridge, not an adjacent chute) before committing, and be alert for rockfall from parties above in this popular, loose corridor.
